review: All six PDF slides and both worksheets inspected; Sheet3 is empty. The architecture on slide 3 is an embedded image and was read visually.

references.finding: Experimental burn-in: 125 C, 168 hours, VCC 4 V, input 3 V. A separate specification row says 300 hours minimum.
references.use: Default 125 C / 168 h / 4 V synthetic demonstration; not a certification requirement.

references.finding: Thermal cycling profile includes approximately -40 C to +60 C, with power states.
references.use: Motivation for time-varying stress. Demo uses a declared sinusoidal profile around 125 C, not this original cycle.

references.finding: Dynamic measurements include temperature, voltage, rise/fall times and propagation delays for multiple device families.
references.use: Propagation delay channel in ns and temperature/voltage covariates. Demo delay baseline 60 ns is illustrative; families are not pooled into a physical device model.

references.finding: T22 capacitor leakage: 6 microamp at 0.0833 h and 0.6 microamp at 770 h, 125 C and 50 V.
references.use: Leakage units and order-of-magnitude context only; these two points are not a degradation curve or a 4 V logic-device specification.

references.finding: Pre/post Vin-High measurements, rather than continuous burn-in time series.
references.use: Motivates change-from-baseline features; no original measurement enters training.

references.finding: Statistical baselines and device-specific voltage limits.
references.use: Motivates separate statistical and specification checks; not used as limits for current or delay.

references.finding: Aggregated reliability tables, including a transistor rate/MTBF inconsistency and headings transcribed as 1250 C.
references.use: Not used to infer failure probabilities, failure prevalence, or model labels.

references.finding: NASA-center screening survey covering thermal and vibration screens.
references.use: Historical screening context only; mechanical testing is outside the slide's software sensor pipeline.

assumptions: All generated telemetry, identities, labels, degradation slopes, noise, correlations, injection times and anomaly prevalence are synthetic.
IDDQ baseline 12 mA, leakage baseline 0.65 microamp, delay baseline 60 ns are prototype assumptions, not NASA-qualified component values.
Demonstration limits: IDDQ 5–22 mA, leakage 0.05–3 microamp, propagation delay 25–100 ns. No hardware qualification claim.
Hourly sampling, default 24-sample trailing window, 24-hour prediction horizon; cycles and supply variation are synthetic.
C_FN=20 and C_FP=1 are relative illustrative costs. Abnormality probability is calibrated on synthetic labels, not mission failure likelihood.
The source gives regression but no exact estimator, covariance metric, fusion formula or hyperparameters. Those choices are documented in METHODS.md.
